channel.title: Defensive Pedal updates
channel.description: What changed on defensivepedal.tech and in the Defensive Pedal cycling navigation app: new figures, new pages, new platforms.

item.title: Guides: starting to cycle in a European city
item.description: One question per page, answered first.

item.title: How do I start cycling to work if traffic scares me?
item.description: Start with the route, not the bike. Traffic is what holds most would-be cyclists back: for every person who rides, about six more would like to. A route on quieter streets is usually only a little longer (Defensive Pedal's routes average about 5% more than the shortest), so ride it on a weekend before your first workday.

item.title: Is it safe to cycle in Austria?
item.description: The 3 ranked cities in Austria average 68.1 out of 100 in the Pedalability Index 2026, against 54.9 across all 300 European cities. Higher score = lower assessed risk. Vienna ranks highest (59th of 300, score 74.6) and Linz lowest (127th, score 59.0). The average is a simple mean of the ranked cities, not weighted by population.

item.title: Country pages, a fuller results table and machine-readable data for the Pedalability Index
item.description: The Pedalability Index now has a page for each of its 31 countries, and its full table lists all 300 cities with country, score, likely range and tier. Higher score = lower assessed risk. The report link is now labelled v1.0, 219 cities. Every page carries the same organisation details, and the site has an llms-full.txt with the methodology and the table as plain text.

item.title: Pedalability Index now in the main menu
item.description: The home page menu now links straight to the Pedalability Index, marked in blue. The same blue marks the link on the cities and consultancies pages.

item.title: Stockholm now scored on the city's measured traffic counts
item.description: Stockholm's score now uses the city's own measured traffic counts instead of modelled traffic. It stays first, at 98.9 instead of 99.0, and its likely range widens from 1st–6th to 1st–8th. Every other city keeps its score; the likely ranges of Haarlem and Brussels now start one place higher.

item.title: Ranking page headline: Pedalability Index 2026: Cycling Risk
item.description: The ranking page now leads with its name, Pedalability Index 2026: Cycling Risk, under the line Data, not Reputation. The ranking itself is unchanged.

item.title: Planning simulator demo video on the cities page
item.description: The cities page now shows a 17-second recording of the planning simulator: a 30 km/h plan for the proposed zero-emission zone in Iași, typed in plain words and re-scored street by street.

item.title: City ranking renamed: Pedalability Index: Cycling Risk
item.description: The 300-city European ranking is now called the Pedalability Index: Cycling Risk and now lives on defensivepedal.tech/pedalability-index. The ranking itself is unchanged; old links redirect.

item.title: The website moved to defensivepedal.tech
item.description: Defensive Pedal's website now lives at defensivepedal.tech. Every old defensivepedal.com address permanently redirects to the same page on the new domain, in English and Romanian. Email addresses are unchanged.

item.title: Homepage validation figure aligned with the published study
item.description: The homepage, methodology page and llms.txt now state the validation result with the exact ratio from the analysis: 2.19 times as many serious injuries per ride on streets rated High risk as on streets rated Safer. The earlier "1 in 5 million vs 1 in 2 million" card is retired. Same change on the Romanian homepage.

item.title: Question-style headings and a cross-page links block on every page
item.description: The homepage, privacy policy and terms now use question headings ("How does Defensive Pedal pick your route?", "Who is responsible for your data?"), open with a one-sentence definition of the app, and end with a links block to every page in both languages plus this feed. Same changes on the Romanian pages.

item.title: Methodology page: how the risk score works and how it was validated
item.description: The seven factor families behind the 100+ risk factors, the data sources, and the validation against crash records at 2,034 sites in five countries: serious-injury rate rises with each risk level, 2.19 times as high on the highest-risk streets. Links the open-access analysis on Zenodo. Also in Romanian at /ro/methodology.

item.title: Privacy policy and terms of use published in English and Romanian
item.description: Full GDPR privacy policy and consumer terms for the app and website: what the app collects and why, retention periods, processors, GDPR rights, Premium billing and the 14-day withdrawal right. Romanian versions at /ro/privacy and /ro/terms.

item.title: Homepage figures updated: 3,984 installs and ETSC 2026 road safety data
item.description: Install count updated to 3,984 across Android and iOS as of October 2026. Safety context now cites ETSC PIN Flash 50 (2026): cyclists are 10% of all people killed on EU roads, 1,926 in 2024, and cyclist deaths fell 8% between 2014 and 2024 while deaths of drivers and passengers fell four times faster.

item.title: European Cycling Risk Ranking of 300 cities linked from the site
item.description: A ranking of 300 European cities by modelled cycling risk, built from the same street-level safety model that powers the app, with a contact block for municipalities on the homepage.

item.title: Defensive Pedal launches on the iOS App Store
item.description: The app is now available for iPhone alongside Android. Safety routing is free on both platforms.
